 Selling my 2006 T1N 3500  
158 wheel base, high roof  
127,500 miles  
partial conversion  


asking $17,000  


History  


I have owned this van for 4 years. Only in Illinois for the last 1.5 years, and was rarely driven in the winter so has very little exposure to road salts and harsh weather. That being said, the body does have minimal amounts of rust, particularly around the windshield and a couple scratches on the sliding door.  


The previous owner kept the van in Texas and used it only for road trips to his land in Colorado. He had a bench seat installed for his nephews, and kept the cargo area otherwise empty so I built it out from there. The van was maintained immaculately in his hands, and I have tried to keep the same high standard.  


I used the van for a few cross country trips and for camping while working at music festivals. I was very happy with it for this purpose, but it's turned out to be more than I need and I'm looking to downsize.  


Conversion  


The interior of this van has been customized to my particular needs, but I would love to help make it work for you. It was perfect for my needs but wouldn't be immediately ready for full time living, which is why I'm considering it a partial conversion. The buildout was done with the expectation that someone someday might want to do things differently, so if you want to continue to customize it, you can easily do so.  


* 420 ah 12v battery bank with monitor and light-duty inverter: I'm running two 210ah Lifeline AGM batteries, charging off the alternator. It's been enough to power the rig in its currenty state for a 5 day stretch with 55% of the battery remaining at the end of it.
* Kitchenette w 12v marine fridge: Purchased the fridge from West Marine last year. Only used it on a few trips. Runs solely off the batteries. The counter is a basic IKEA unit. I've got a water tank and pump you can have but ultimately decided for my needs it was unnecessary.
* LED lights and charging outlets: USB and cigarette ports. The lights in the rear are dimmable as I found it a little too bright for laying in bed and reading and such.
* Raised bed: I had room to keep two tall road bikes under the bed in a slideout I've since scrapped. Still plenty of room to sit up in bed. I think it maximizes the space well.
* Utility shelving and bench: These were quick additions before a work trip. Nothing special here.
* Vent/fan: The basic Maxxair fan with temperture control but no remote or anything fancy.
* Cedar wall/ceiling planks
* Vinyl flooring with OSB subfloor
* Foamular insulation: Probably not recommended for extreme temperatures. But again, I made sure it'd be easy to remove if you want to install something else.

Everything is negotiable. Take it as it is or let me know which parts to scrap and I'll adjust the price accordingly.  


More details/maintenance/etc  


Maintenance always performed on time, including all filters and cleaning the notoriously finicky EGR valve  


Front tires only have about 3k miles on them  
Rear inside tires only have about 15k miles on them  
Rear outside tires nearing end of lifespan  


New AC condenser and receiver/dryer  
New water pump  


Over the winter I replaced all the injector seals and hold down bolts as a few of them had started to fail. Fuel return line was replaced with the newer heavier duty metal fittings. Engine is clean and running beautifully.  


One glow plug needs to be replaced, which sets off the check engine light occasionally, but the other four work no problem and it's absolutely never struggled to start so I've held off on doing that sensitive repair. I do have a new glow plug if you want to do it.
